acceptance_evidence: CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.
completion_conditions: A plan task entry that declares a cca_checklist_profile registers a task carrying it verbatim, and MergeGate's coverage gate then blocks a verdict that omits a declared id.
`shiki issue plan` can declare a checklist profile and records it on the task it registers.
A task registered with no declared profile carries [] - present, empty, and behaviourally identical to today for MergeGate.
A binder test asserts that the two registration paths emit the same task-record key set, so a future field added to one path alone fails immediately instead of silently.

decisions: THE DEFECT, MEASURED. `grep -c cca_checklist_profile scripts/shiki_tasks.py` returns 0: the field is not part of task registration at all. Driving register_task_from_plan directly against a temp target on 2026-08-22, a plan entry declaring ["CCA-01","CCA-09"] produced a task file whose keys were exactly acceptance_checks, assigned_runtime, dependencies, expected_branch, expected_pr, github_issue, goal_id, id, ledger_evidence, locks, non_goals, required_skills, risk_level, scope, status, test_command, title - no cca_checklist_profile. A plan entry declaring [] produced the same absent key. The shipped record .shiki/tasks/T-20260822T100310256523Z-ca34e786.json, registered by merged Contract PR #337 from plan P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792 whose task entry declares [], confirms this is shipped behaviour on real state rather than a one-off.

THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE. mergegate_check.checklist_profile_coverage_failures is the field's only consumer, and it returns no reasons when the profile is absent OR empty. Measured against a verdict judging only CCA-02: the registered task yielded [], the same task with the profile carried yielded two blocking reasons naming CCA-01 and CCA-09. A planner who declares a required checklist profile today therefore gets exactly zero enforcement, and nothing anywhere reports the loss. This is the governance failure the fix removes; the [] default (decision 5) is inert by comparison.

THE REPORT'S PREMISE, CORRECTED - AND WHY SCOPE COVERS BOTH PATHS. The bug report states that cmd_issue_plan 'does accept and write it, so the two task-creation paths disagree'. It does not. cmd_issue_plan's payload (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:946-966) omits the field, and the `issue plan` subparser (scripts/shiki_cli.py:347-362) declares no --cca-checklist-profile flag. Both paths drop it identically. All nine task files in the mirror that carry a profile got it by hand: T-20260807T073307221254Z-2d22d654 carried its twelve ids in its very first commit b635454 'chore(shiki): register SADR namespace contract', a hand-written registration, and the other eight carry bare family names ["PR","TDD","V","CCA"] that no verdict item id can ever match. Fixing only the plan path would CREATE the divergence the report believed already existed. Operator decision 2026-08-22: cover both paths, adding the CLI flag.

BINDING THE PAIR - THE INVARIANT THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS. Measured: register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan emit byte-identical task-record key sets today - the same seventeen keys, set difference empty in both directions - and nothing asserts it. That is precisely the unbound-pair shape tests/test_paired_invariants.py exists to remove: two artifacts that must agree with nothing binding them, so a break is silent. The new test therefore pins SET-EQUALITY of the two paths' key sets rather than merely checking that each carries the profile: a containment check passes while one path silently gains a field the other lacks, which is this defect exactly. Each assertion is paired with a divergence test that mutates one side and proves the binder fails, per the convention in that module's docstring.

DEFAULT IS [] AND THE DEFAULT IS INERT. checklist_profile_coverage_failures returns no reasons for an absent profile and none for an empty one, so writing [] where nothing was declared changes no MergeGate outcome for any task - it only makes a DECLARED profile bite. [] is also the only safe default: the eight legacy records carrying bare family names ('PR', 'TDD', 'V', 'CCA') show what a non-empty default would do, because a family name is not a verdict item id and would block every PR that inherited it.

NOT PROMOTED TO REQUIRED, AND WHY. The report asks whether validate_shiki and MergeGate should require the field before the default changes. They should not, yet. 141 of the mirror's 150 task files lack it (re-counted at origin/main dd8d5c9; it was 136 of 145 when the requirements were drafted). scripts/validate_shiki.py keeps it out of TASK_REQUIRED and .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json keeps it out of `required`, both carrying comments stating that promotion needs the whole corpus backfilled and that the two surfaces must be promoted TOGETHER - bound by tests/test_cca_verdict_consistency.TaskSchemaRequiredConsistency. Backfilling .shiki/tasks/** is a migration-mode concern outside this slice's locks. What this task does is make the field present on every NEW registration, which is the precondition any later promotion needs.

CONTRACT MODE DOES NOT BIND IT EITHER - DEFERRED WITH A MEASUREMENT. mergegate_check._FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS (scripts/mergegate_check.py:396) does not list cca_checklist_profile, so _frozen_task_match_errors returned [] both for the dropped-profile case and for the plan-declares-[]-task-absent case. Adding it would be the durable binder, but it must not land here: the live goal G-20260822T100310254979Z-b0f195ee has a frozen plan declaring [] against a registered task with the field absent, so the rule would flag it immediately. That goal is now complete and its implementation PR #339 merged, but the mismatch itself persists in the mirror, and 141 task files lack the field, so the non-goal rests on the corpus mismatch rather than on an open PR. This is recorded as a non-goal and a follow-up to be sequenced after a mirror backfill.

ADJACENT SILENT DROP, DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. The same function reads task_plan.get('runtime') (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:340), but plan P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792 declares 'assigned_runtime': 'claude' on its task entry. Measured: the registered task T-20260822T100310256523Z-ca34e786 has assigned_runtime 'claude-code' - the plan's value was ignored and the default silently applied. It was harmless only by luck, since 'claude' is not in task.schema.json's assigned_runtime enum and would have failed validation had it been carried; and _frozen_task_match_errors skips its runtime comparison entirely when frozen.get('runtime') is falsy, so a plan meaning 'codex' would dispatch to the wrong runtime unnoticed. Same defect class, different fix (key naming, schema enum, plan-guide contract). Operator decision 2026-08-22: separate follow-up slice, not folded in. Accordingly this plan's own task entry uses the 'runtime' key the code actually reads.

RISK IS LOW AND THE ARCHITECTURE GATE IS NOT TRIGGERED. Two payload lines, one argparse flag, and one new test file: no schema change, no workflow, no migration, no auth, no public API or infrastructure surface; well under 100 net new lines in a core module; three files touched, one of them new. .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json already declares the property, so nothing about the task record's contract changes - only whether the field is populated. Low and medium both take the autonomous SADR-0008/SADR-0009 merge path, so this classification does not change the loop route.

MEASURED GREEN BEFORE FREEZE. The candidate change was applied in the planning worktree purely to measure lock sufficiency, then reverted, so this contract registers no implementation. With both registration paths and the CLI flag changed: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, run in five alphabetical chunks to stay within this session's command limits, gave 327 + 214 + 409 + 92 + 128 = 1170 tests, OK in every chunk; `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .` gave 'Shiki validation passed'; and scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh, test_shiki_run_orchestrator.sh, test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh, test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh, test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh, test_shiki_evidence_integrity.sh, test_shiki_state_classes.sh, test_shiki_manifest.sh, test_shiki_validator_hardening.sh, test_shiki_doctor.sh and test_shiki_p2_schema_drift.sh all PASS. `shiki issue plan --help` listed the new --cca-checklist-profile option. The remaining scripts/test_shiki_*.sh were not run locally and are left to CI.

LOCK SUFFICIENCY. MUST-CHANGE is scripts/shiki_tasks.py (both payloads), scripts/shiki_cli.py (the flag) and the new tests/test_plan_task_carry.py; the measured green run changed nothing else. MUST-NOT-BREAK is the full Python suite, validate_shiki and the scripts/test_shiki_*.sh set, which are verification commands rather than lock entries. The tests directory ships wholesale via shiki_installer.TEMPLATE_PATHS, so a new test file needs no installer change and no TARGET_INSTALL_EXCLUDES entry - provided it stays target-valid, which it does by building temp-directory targets and importing only shipped modules. Three locks are therefore sufficient and no lock-widening amendment should be needed.

REGISTRATION BLOCKERS - ONE CLEARED, ONE REMAINING. When the requirements were drafted on 2026-08-22, has_active_lock_conflict returned one conflict: path:scripts/shiki_tasks.py held by T-20260817T063758155247Z-0b11207b, whose status was 'review' although its expected_pr #335 was merged - loop closeout drift, not a live claim. That has since resolved on its own: the goal loop closed the task out through PR #343, it is now status 'done' with its lock record state 'released', and a scan of every ACTIVE lock record at origin/main dd8d5c9 finds nothing overlapping this task's three locks. The remaining blocker is the Contract PR queue: #340 and #341 are open, both carrying guardian:approved and mergegate:contract, and the repository's measured choreography admits one Contract PR at a time. Operator decision 2026-08-22: draft now, hold ingest and the Contract PR until that queue clears. Nothing in the mirror was mutated to work around either blocker.

CI-08 DEVIATION, DECLARED. Context and Impact here was produced by direct exploration in this session rather than by a Workflow parallel exploration sweep, because this session's operator configuration prohibits Workflow and subagent dispatch. Every claim above is a first-hand measurement in worktree nifty-meninsky-14246c rather than a delegated summary, but the CI-08 sweep-run evidence does not exist for this Goal and should not be claimed.

RE-VERIFIED AT FREEZE. The requirements were drafted 2026-08-22 at 071b707 and frozen 2026-08-24, so every claim was re-checked against origin/main dd8d5c9 first. The code surfaces are byte-identical: `git diff 071b707 origin/main` over scripts/shiki_tasks.py, scripts/shiki_cli.py, scripts/mergegate_check.py, scripts/validate_shiki.py, .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json and .shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json reports no change, so the defect reproduction and the measured-green run stand unmodified and were not re-run. Three mirror-derived numbers moved and are corrected in the decisions above: the corpus is now 141 of 150 task files lacking the field; goal G-20260822T100310254979Z-b0f195ee is complete and PR #339 merged, though its registered task still lacks the field its frozen plan declares; and the scripts/shiki_tasks.py lock blocker has cleared. No claim in this plan is carried forward unmeasured across the two-day gap.
grill_with_docs.source: Claude Code planning session 2026-08-22 in worktree nifty-meninsky-14246c, from an operator bug report. Every claim below was re-measured first-hand in that worktree rather than taken from the report; three of the report's statements did not survive measurement and are corrected in decisions 3, 7 and 8.

non_goals: Promoting cca_checklist_profile to a required field in scripts/validate_shiki.py TASK_REQUIRED or .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json `required`. Measured: 136 of 145 task files lack it, both surfaces carry comments saying promotion must be joint and needs a corpus backfill, and .shiki/tasks/** is outside this task's locks.
Backfilling the existing .shiki/tasks records. Mirror rewrites are a migration-mode concern with a byte-identity constraint; this task changes only what NEW registrations write.

Adding cca_checklist_profile to mergegate_check._FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS. Measured: it would immediately block goal G-20260822T100310254979Z-b0f195ee, whose frozen plan declares [] against a registered task lacking the field, and whose implementation PR #339 is open.
Fixing the plan-entry `runtime` versus `assigned_runtime` key mismatch measured in the same function. Same defect class, different fix; operator decided 2026-08-22 to take it as a separate slice.
Changing checklist_profile_coverage_failures, TERMINAL_CHECKLIST_STATUSES, or any other MergeGate semantics. The consumer is correct; only the producer was silent.

Adding cca_checklist_profile to .shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json's task-item properties. Plan task items already permit it through additionalProperties: true, and four plans in the mirror declare it today.
Repairing the stale lock on scripts/shiki_tasks.py or the drifted status of T-20260817T063758155247Z-0b11207b. Recorded as a registration blocker for the operator or the loop, not fixed here.
outcome: Every task Shiki registers carries the CCA checklist profile its plan or its operator declared, so MergeGate's coverage gate actually enforces it. Measured 2026-08-22 in worktree nifty-meninsky-14246c at 071b707: register_task_from_plan given a plan task entry declaring cca_checklist_profile ["CCA-01","CCA-09"] wrote a task file with the key entirely absent. mergegate_check.checklist_profile_coverage_failures(registered_task, {"checklist":[{"id":"CCA-02","status":"pass"}]}) then returned [], while the identical call on the same task with the profile carried returned ['CCA checklist profile id CCA-01 is missing from the verdict checklist', 'CCA checklist profile id CCA-09 is missing from the verdict checklist']. The coverage gate is therefore a no-op for every plan-registered task, while AGENTS.md 'Goal, PRD, and Task Requirements' states that every executable task must include a CCA checklist profile.
title: Carry the declared CCA checklist profile into every registered task
